topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as the evolution of mutation-bearing cells whose progression depends on their biological context.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer occurrence can be attributed to environmental exposures rather than simply to chance or inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to carcinogenesis, developing Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage and mutations through their activity within the body.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutation-bearing cells may require a growth-promoting environment before tumours develop.

topics.label: Context-dependent carcinogen susceptibility and mechanistic summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological context shapes carcinogen effects and conclude by synthesising the mechanisms discussed.

topics.label: Methods and limitations for identifying cancer-causing exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence researchers can obtain to connect exposures with cancer and the limitations of that evidence.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by recapping its conclusions and framing their implications for everyday risk–benefit decisions.
